speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, has your baby been breathing normally since birth, or did the difficulty start immediately after delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your baby was born at 33 weeks and developed distress two hours after birth, have you noticed any signs like grunting, nasal flaring, or a "see-saw" chest movement?

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Gases: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L; Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the ABG showing respiratory acidosis and the chest X-ray revealing ground-glass opacities in a 33-week premature infant, I am highly suspecting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). Are there any other symptoms, such as cyanosis or retractions, and what is the baby's current heart rate?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
